quick_skim.title: Representation Learning via Composite Subspace Flow Matching
quick_skim.abstract: Distilling semantic meaning from raw image data remains a challenge in machine learning. Current self-supervised paradigms face a trade-off: joint-embedding architectures produce relevant features by aggressively discarding intra-class variance, irreversibly spatial and reconstruction. Conversely, generative models preserve spatial details but struggle to isolate semantics, as their optimization is dominated by pixel variations. To bridge this divide, we propose composite subspace flow matching (CSFM). Rather than corrupting data with unstructured isotropic noise, CSFM formulates representation learning as the variance-minimizing inversion of a deterministic degradation curriculum across spectral, color, and illumination subspaces. By bounding trajectory variance with hard temporal style truncation, a capacity-constrained encoder is driven to ignore transient style artifacts and encode persistent content. Empirical evaluations across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and STL-10 show that CSFM yields competitive discriminative transferability while preserving generative synthesis across both convolutional and vision transformer architectures. By avoiding the collapse pathologies of non-generative methods, CSFM forms a smooth latent space that outperforms standard optimal transport flows on linear probing and few-shot classification, while enabling coherent synthesis and trajectory interpolation. These results confirm that steering the physical dynamics of generative flows offers a scalable paradigm for learning representations that are simultaneously linearly separable and generatively invertible.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 针对自监督表示学习中联合嵌入丢弃类内方差、生成模型又难以分离语义的问题,本文提出复合子空间流匹配CSFM。方法不再用各向同性噪声破坏数据,而是把表示学习建模为跨频谱、颜色与光照子空间的确定性退化课程的方差最小化逆过程。实验表明该方法在保留空间细节的同时更好地分离语义。其贡献在于用流匹配桥接了生成与判别式表示学习。

quick_skim.title: PRIME W0: Physical Priors from World Models for Embodied Manipulation
quick_skim.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models excel at instruction following, yet most remain feed-forward: they condition actions only on the current observation and discard both long-horizon temporal context and the hierarchical structure of VLM representations. We present PRIME W0, a hierarchical conditional flow-matching framework that closes this gap through three synergistic designs: (1)per-layer KV injection from a pretrained VLM into an Adaptive MoE action expert; (2)dynamics-aware conditioning via asynchronous world-model subgoal-image prediction and a DINOv2 historical-frame semantic bridge; and (3)Action Dynamic Manifold (ADM) flow matching with covariance-structured noise that respects robot kinematic coupling. PRIME W0 is trained in four stages---VLM pre-training, DAT/NTP visuomotor pre-training, DiT flow-matching decoder assembly with WM injection, and end-to-end SFT---and achieves state-of-the-art results on LIBERO and real-robot benchmarks, with systematic ablations validating each architectural component.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 针对视觉语言动作模型仅依赖当前观测、丢弃长时程时序上下文与层次结构的问题,本文提出分层条件流匹配框架PRIME W0。方法将VLM逐层KV注入自适应MoE动作专家,并通过世界模型子目标图像与历史语义桥接提供动态感知条件,同时采用符合机器人运动耦合的协方差结构化流匹配噪声。实验表明该框架提升了具身操作表现。其贡献在于把流匹配与层次化世界模型先验结合用于动作生成。

quick_skim.title: Learning Safe Flow Matching Robot Policies from Binary Feasibility Oracles
quick_skim.abstract: Robot foundation models increasingly rely on flow-based action generation for general-purpose manipulation, yet the generated actions are not guaranteed to satisfy physical constraints such as joint limits and collision avoidance. This problem is especially challenging when the feasible set cannot be described analytically and is accessible only through black-box feasibility oracles. We study this practical oracle-only setting and propose an oracle-guided differentiable safeguard for safe flow-matching robot policies. The safeguard uses binary feasibility queries to correct unsafe updates in the forward pass, while extracting local boundary information to provide constraint-aware learning signals in the backward pass. Combined with discrete-time flow matching, the same safeguard is used during training and inference, enabling forward--backward aligned policy learning without explicit or differentiable constraint models. Experiments on obstacle-aware robotic manipulation demonstrate 100% constraint satisfaction while preserving task performance.
